Negotiating an ownership transition for a software business

Identifying a buyer and negotiating terms intended to meet the objectives of employees and founders.

The objective

An Indian software services company, specialising in application development and maintenance on the AS/400 platform, had about 300 trained engineers. Demand was growing, but retaining talent had become a challenge and the business could not scale to meet it. Several services companies were interested in acquiring it. The founders sought an exit in which employees would receive better packages and the founders good value.

Shyam’s contribution

Shyam identified the buyer and negotiated an agreement with it on terms intended to meet these objectives.

Where it stood

Agreement on the proposed transition was reached with the buyer. Completion of the transaction is not confirmed in Shyam’s account, and the improvements sought for employees and founders were objectives of the negotiation, not reported results.

Source: Shyam Sundar Pani’s account.

The experience this brings

Finding the right counterparty and negotiating terms that reflect what owners and employees need from a transition.

Related services

  • Plan for succession and renewal
  • Develop workable agreements

Linked as transferable experience, not as a Japan–India assignment.
